methods.label: Test the laws using the definition
methods.explanation:
The definition gives \(x*y=xy+x+y\). A statement claimed for all real inputs is false if even one allowed substitution fails. In B, take \(x=1\) and \(y=z=0\). Since \(1*0=(1+1)(0+1)-1=1\), we get
\[1*(0+0)=1,\qquad (1*0)+(1*0)=2.\]
Thus B is false.

To verify that it is the only false choice, consider the other statements. A holds because \(xy+x+y=yx+y+x\). D holds because \(x*0=(x+1)\cdot1-1=x\).

For C, applying the definition to each side gives
\[(x-1)*(x+1)=x(x+2)-1=x^2+2x-1,\]
and
\[(x*x)-1=(x+1)^2-2=x^2+2x-1.\]
Thus C holds.

For E, the useful form of the definition is \((u*v)+1=(u+1)(v+1)\), valid for all real \(u,v\). Applying it to the inner operation gives
\[x*(y*z)=(x+1)(y+1)(z+1)-1,\]
and
\[(x*y)*z=(x+1)(y+1)(z+1)-1.\]
These expressions agree, so E holds as well. The false statement is choice B.
